questions.story: International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Finland–Russia relations, Norway–Russia relations
questions.question: Which country recently announced visa restrictions prohibiting Russian athletes from entering the country for sports competitions?
questions.explanation: Finland implemented new visa bans preventing Russian competitors from coming to the nation for sporting events.
questions.context: International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Finland–Russia relations, Norway–Russia relations: Finland announces visa restrictions preventing Russian athletes, including neutral competitors, from entering for sporting events beginning November 16. Norway also announces similar restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes and their support staff.

questions.question: Which major technology company saw its chief executive step down following reports of extramarital affairs involving a suspected foreign spy?
questions.explanation: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia as CEO and board member amid reports concerning his personal relationships.
questions.context: Jensen Huang spying scandal: Jensen Huang resigns as chief executive officer (CEO) and president of Nvidia and leaves the company's board following reports of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese intelligence agent. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO.

questions.question: Which television network's journalists were targeted in a London espionage plot that led to convictions in a British court?
questions.explanation: Two men were convicted by a UK court for spying on journalists working for the London-based outlet Iran International.
questions.context: Iranian external operations: A British court convicts two Iranian men of spying on journalists from London-based broadcaster Iran International. One of them is also convicted of preparing a violent attack, while a third defendant is acquitted.

questions.question: Which disease has tragically caused over 1,200 child fatalities in an ongoing outbreak in Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: A severe outbreak of measles in Bangladesh has claimed the lives of more than 1,299 children.
questions.context: 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak: Four more children in Bangladesh are reported to have died from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,299.

questions.question: What was the name of the global Europol operation targeting illicit dark web marketplaces that led to hundreds of arrests?
questions.explanation: Operation TorNado was an international law enforcement crackdown resulting in 354 arrests and the seizure of cash and contraband.
questions.context: Europol announces that Operation TorNado, an international investigation into illegal dark web marketplaces, resulted in 354 arrests across 14 countries and the seizure of approximately 5.7 tonnes of drugs, 209 firearms, and €211 million (US$234 million) in assets.
